g_policy.reason: The offer is an opt-in card. The offer copy states the reward (priority routing for 60 minutes) before the game. Declining leaves the menu unchanged, and the 'if the ad fails' field covers both no game available and a play that isn't verified.

g_no_cash.reason: The reward is 60 minutes of queue priority, which cannot be withdrawn, sold or transferred.

g_no_chat_content.reason: The trigger event says the card only goes to users 'whose chats are mostly long roleplay stories'. That targeting depends on chat content (topics and genre), not an app event.

g_no_free_removal.reason: Nothing free is removed or capped. The idea only adds a temporary priority boost.

g_brand_safety.reason: The card sits in the profile menu drawer (s09), a sheet over the non-chat Profile screen, and s09 is rated safe. It is not in or next to a conversation.

c1_revealed_value.reason: Priority routing is a resource the app charges for, as shown by the paywall bullet l02 'Priority routing for faster replies' (s02.e06).

c2_evidence.reason: The proposal assumes free users wait in a normal queue and that 'replies keep their normal speed'. The model only infers this (m03), and its open questions say the free-tier queue priority was not observed. The behavior after the user returns from the Upgrade entry was also never captured, and neither was the 'mostly long roleplay' user segment.

c4_protects_subscription.reason: The reward is a 60-minute sample, capped at 2 per day. It leaves the subscription's always-on priority, 5× context and extra swipes intact.

c5_moment.reason: The card is on the profile menu, a persistent surface the user chooses to open, and it appears after they looked at Upgrade. It does not interrupt a task in progress.

c6_fits_simula.reason: This is a play-to-earn unit, and the reward is granted after the game is played and verified. The trigger is an app event (returning to the profile menu from the Upgrade entry).

c7_specific.reason: It names Janitor+ priority routing (s02.e06), the profile menu's Upgrade entry (s09.e31), and the Billing neighbor, so it would not read the same in another app.

other_concern: The reward's value rests on a free-tier queue that was never observed. Whether the Upgrade entry opens another screen the user returns from is also unobserved. The sponsored game and priority card are new screens, but that is normal for this unit.
